steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
Here’s a rapid rundown of the main differences between RNA and DNA:

1. Sugar backbone  
   • DNA contains deoxyribose (lacks one oxygen atom)  
   • RNA contains ribose (has one more oxygen)

2. Nitrogenous bases  
   • DNA uses adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C) and guanine (G)  
   • RNA uses adenine (A), uracil (U) instead of thymine, plus cytosine (C) and guanine (G)

3. Strand structure  
   • DNA is typically double-stranded, forming a stable double helix  
   • RNA is usually single-stranded and can fold into varied 3D shapes

4. Function  
   • DNA stores and transmits genetic information in the nucleus (and mitochondria)  
   • RNA translates that code into proteins (mRNA), helps assemble amino acids (tRNA, rRNA), and regulates gene expression

5. Stability and location  
   • DNA is more chemically stable, long-term storage in the nucleus  
   • RNA is less stable, found in nucleus and cytoplasm, often short-lived

That’s the core of it—sugar, bases, structure, function and stability.
